issue_paraphrase: Searching a file with ripgrep's multiline mode (-U) together with a replacement string (-r/--replace) can crash the program outright when the pattern yields many small matches: ripgrep aborts with a panic about an invalid slice index and exits non-zero instead of printing the replaced lines. fix_summary: In the replacer (crates/printer/src/util.rs), a match's end can legitimately exceed the reported range end for multiline look-around cases; the code then sliced bytes[last_match..end] with start > end, panicking. The fix sets the end to bytes.len() when last_match > range.end.
notes: No pcre2 feature needed; default cargo build is enough. Debug and release builds both crash at parent. issue_paraphrase: Hidden files that are explicitly re-included through a whitelist rule in an ignore file (for example '!.foo.txt') are still skipped when the search starts inside a subdirectory and the search path is given as '.'. ripgrep then reports no results at all even though the whitelisted hidden file should be searched, while the same search from the parent directory - or with the path spelled without a dot - works correctly.
fix_summary: In the ancestor-ignore walker (crates/ignore/src/dir.rs), when a parent ignore's directory is exactly '.', the code proceeded to strip leading './' and '/' off relative paths, mangling hidden file names and causing whitelisted hidden files to be filtered out. The fix returns the path unchanged when the parent dir is '.', preserving hidden names like '.foo.txt'.
notes: No pcre2, no network. The subtlety is that the bug appears only for the '.' search-path spelling from a subdirectory; a good task should contrast all six invocation forms from the regression test (which is in tests/regression.rs as r3173_hidden_whitelist_only_dot) so the agent cannot pass by chance.

issue_paraphrase: Certain regular expressions that combine case-insensitivity with alternation silently find nothing when they should match: for example a pattern like '(?i:e.x|ex)' reports zero matches against a file containing the string 'e-x', even though the pattern unambiguously matches it. ripgrep exits successfully with no results and no error message, so the missed matches are easy to overlook and hard to diagnose.
fix_summary: regex inner-literal extraction: when two extracted literal sequences are unioned, prefix is now set to true only when both operands have prefix true, and choose() always returns an inexact sequence. issue_paraphrase: Searching files with CRLF line endings while color output is forced on ('--crlf' together with '--color=always') makes ripgrep crash on certain inputs - a file containing just a newline is enough. It dies with an arithmetic/index-out-of-bounds panic and a non-zero exit code without printing the matched line, in both debug and release builds.
fix_summary: printer (crates/printer/src/standard.rs): when looking back one byte to trim a CR in --crlf mode, the code indexed buf[end-1] without checking end == 0, so an empty line under the `x?`-style pattern underflowed the index. The fix uses a bounds-checked buf.get(end-1) that treats out-of-range as no CR.
notes: Crash reproduces in debug AND release builds (message differs: overflow vs index OOB), so the author can use either profile. Golden test r1765 (in tests/regression.rs) simply asserts non-empty stdout; the direct panic-vs-match comparison above is a sharper oracle. Requires --crlf --color always as in the test; without those flags the bad path is not reached.

issue_paraphrase: Running ripgrep with word matching enabled ('-w/--word-regexp') against a pattern that can match the empty string (an empty pattern is the simplest example) crashes partway through: it prints the first match and then aborts with an internal assertion failure and a non-zero exit code instead of reporting all of the word-boundary match positions. fix_summary: The -w fast path wrapped the pattern in word-boundary assertions at the matcher level (crates/matcher/src/lib.rs), and the resulting empty match produced a matcher range with start > end, tripping an assertion. The fix reworked the word-boundary handling in crates/regex/src/word.rs so empty matches at word boundaries are emitted correctly.
